slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch, packaging and price

paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch, packaging and price
Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Synthetic benchmark data: fictional company; all figures from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not as a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of ARR, not $8M
Copilot is worth launching: it improved beta productivity and renewals, and Routewise has made AI part of the buying decision
–	Beta jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11%, against 2% for matched accounts
–	Our win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37% after it bundled AI
The prize is a third of what the plan assumes: real purchases point to about $2.5M of add-on ARR, not $8M
–	Only 14% of beta accounts paid, against 46% survey intent
–	Win-back from Routewise is worth at most $0.6M a year
Package Copilot in Pro at $12 more per seat with a fair-use allowance, rather than as a flat $149 add-on
–	Pro closes the NRR gap if 26% move up; our 2023 tier drew 33%
–	A fair-use allowance keeps gross margin above the 75% floor
The real cost is the two-quarter mobile delay, yet launching still adds about $2.4M of net ARR under five conditions
–	Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, against 6% for AI
–	Even with the delay at its ceiling, Pro adds about $2.4M net

Both risks are counted at their ceiling
▪	Pro ARR: 9,800 accounts × 33% × $893 premium a year, with movers at the average 6.2 seats
▪	Mobile delay: $57.6M ARR × 14% churn × 27% citing mobile × half a year, as if the rewrite would end all mobile churn
▪	Not netted: the one-time $1.47M of engineering (14 of our 60 engineers for two quarters at $210,000 a year)
▪	The mobile delay could cost up to 38% of Pro's first-year ARR, so the rewrite's new date must hold
The delay is worth accepting only with the rewrite's new date and team locked before launch
